final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the interpretation of the same record. That reframing is partly correct: the evidence does not support clean certification based on rollout controls alone. But it still does not close the initial support gaps. Concern accounting remains unchanged: the weak tax filing assistant segment is still exposed; the random 8% gate does not exclude that use case; the only risk-acceptance artifact is an unapproved draft that does not address the exposure; and there is still no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has actually been completed before launch. Under the policy text, rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate only if they exclude the affected use case or include reviewed risk acceptance; neither condition is met here. A promise to disclose, a caveated framing, or a proposal to treat the issue as monitored does not itself satisfy the unresolved compliance predicate. This is therefore not supportable as compliant or compliant_with_caveats on the present record, but the record is stronger than outright noncompliance because the failure shown is primarily missing proof of required launch conditions rather than decisive evidence that launch occurred without them.
remaining_concerns: The affected tax filing assistant segment remains below target and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by filing cohort, so rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the tax filing assistant exposure.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed or formally committed before launch.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one incidents, staged rollout, monitoring, and rollback do not satisfy the policy predicate for an exposed material limitation.
